headline: Spot vol broke 8.6% lower and the dollar paused — but the liquidation simply moved offshore, into Brazil and into the miners.
summary: Yesterday the story was credit cracking. Today credit didn't move (HY still 3.43, CCC 13.29, IG 0.92, BBB 1.15 — all dated 11/17) and the front of the vol curve healed: VIX -8.6% to 22.44, now back below VIX3M at 24.29, MOVE -3.6% to 94.66 and -6.9% on the month. DXY actually fell 0.2% to 103.62, EURUSD +0.1%, USDKRW -0.4%, USDCNY -0.1%. If you only watched the US index screen you'd call today a stabilisation. You'd be wrong. The stress didn't disappear, it emigrated: USDBRL +2.1% to 5.897, now +17.1% in a month at a one-month z of 4.78 with acceleration z=3.64 — the single most violent series on the board — after yesterday's pause. EWZ -3.1% to 30.07, -28.3% on the month (z=-3.62, acceleration -3.36), 0th percentile of its 52-week range; Bovespa -19.4% monthly. USDMXN added another 2.6% and sits at the 100th percentile, EWW -4.2%, ARGT -2.3% and -20.5% on the month. CEW -0.7%. This is no longer a broad dollar story; it is a LatAm funding story inside a flat dollar.

The second migration is inside hard assets, and it is the equity, not the metal, that is being sold. Copper actually rose 0.4% today and gold only fell 0.9% — yet COPX -6.3% (-23.2% on the month, z=-2.47), FCX -7.0%, GDX -6.0%, GDXJ -6.0%, NEM -6.0%, EZA -5.5%. GDX/gold -2.9%. That is forced de-grossing of levered resource equity, not a commodity view. Same pattern in energy, in the other direction: WTI +0.6% to 83.73 while XLE -3.3%, XOP -3.4%, XOM -4.0%, CVX -4.0% — oil equities finally catching down to a tape where crude is -17.7% and gasoline -20.0% on the month. And Asia tech took another leg: TAIEX -4.4% to 38,427, -17.0% on the month at z=-3.11 with acceleration -1.76; EWT -11.4% on the week; SMH -16.2% monthly with SMH/SPY at z=-2.01; NVDA -30.5% on the month and pinned at the 0th percentile. Single-stock gap risk is live too — UNH -10.2% in one session dragged XLV -2.2%.

The offsets are getting stronger, not weaker, and they all run through the consumer. Gasoline -20.0% and WTI -17.7% on the month is a direct rebate: XRT +2.3% today with XRT/SPY at z=1.86, XLY +1.8%, TGT +4.0%, AMZN +3.8%, XLY/XLP +2.1%, UPS +15.6% and MCD +12.9% on the month. Mortgages at 7.11%, -29bp monthly with acceleration z=-2.36, have ITB +9.1% and XHB/SPY at z=2.24. Breadth keeps refusing to confirm the index damage: equal-weight/cap-weight +6.0% on the month at z=2.89 with acceleration 1.83, transports/S&P z=2.76 acceleration 2.06, small caps/S&P z=1.48 acceleration 1.91, RUT +0.5%. Labour is intact — claims 203k, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), unemployment 4.1%. And leadership is clearly identifiable: Sensex +12.4% on the month (z=2.95, acceleration 2.27), INDA relative strength +14.0%, helped by USDINR -1.8% on cheap crude.

The rates math is unchanged and still the binding constraint. The 3-month bill at 4.33% is 45bp above effective fed funds at 3.88%; 2s at 4.80%, 10s at 5.10% (+12bp on the week), 30s at 5.46%. But 10-year breakevens are 2.19 at the 3rd percentile (z=-1.10) and 5-year 2.23, so the 10-year real yield at 2.89% sits at the 95th percentile, 27.9% above its 200-day. Nominal stickiness plus collapsing breakevens is passive tightening, and 2s10s at 27bp with acceleration -1.02 is flattening to confirm it. Inflation composite 54 against a growth pulse of -10 is the tension. Net: risk regime improved marginally to -17 from -19, dollar composite -52 from -53, rates -50 from -51 — but the improvement is cosmetic. Tails are being sold into a widening spread cycle (SKEW 142.84, -11.8% on the month at z=-1.78, acceleration -1.92) while HY sits at the 94th percentile. Own the disinflation consumer and the belly of the curve; short the levered periphery and the resource equity; do not buy the bounce in high beta (SPHB/SPLV -13.5% monthly, z=-2.13).

good.text: Vol curve repaired: VIX -8.6% to 22.44, now back under VIX3M at 24.29; MOVE -3.6% to 94.66 and -6.9% on the month. The panic bid in protection has drained.

Breadth is accelerating away from the index damage: equal-weight/cap-weight +6.0% monthly at z=2.89 (acc 1.83), transports/S&P z=2.76 (acc 2.06), small caps/S&P z=1.48 (acc 1.91), equal-weight S&P still in an uptrend.
The energy rebate is landing in the consumer tape: gasoline -20.0% on the month, XRT +2.3% today, XLY +1.8%, TGT +4.0%, AMZN +3.8%, WMT +7.3% and COST +10.3% monthly.
Housing is re-rating off lower mortgage rates — 7.11%, -29bp on the month with acceleration z=-2.36; ITB +9.1% monthly, XHB +1.7% today, XHB/SPY z=2.24.
Labour still won't break: initial claims 203k, continuing claims 1.763m, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), unemployment 4.1% and falling. No recession signal in the hard data.
Clear surviving leadership: Sensex +12.4% on the month (z=2.95, acc 2.27), INDA relative strength +14.0%/+9.1%, with USDINR -1.8% as cheap crude feeds the terms of trade.

bad.text: Brazil is in a disorderly move: USDBRL +2.1% to 5.897, +17.1% monthly at z=4.78 with acceleration 3.64 — the most extreme series on the board; EWZ -28.3% on the month (z=-3.62) at the 0th percentile; Bovespa -19.4%.
The contagion is regional, not idiosyncratic: USDMXN +2.6% and at the 100th percentile, EWW -4.2%, MXX -1.8%, ARGT -2.3% (-20.5% monthly), EM currency basket -1.2% on the week at z=-1.19.

Credit never recovered from yesterday's crack: HY OAS 3.43 at the 94th percentile (+68bp in three months), CCC 13.29 (+302bp 3m), IG 0.92 at z=1.04 and BBB 1.15 at z=1.11; HYG/IEF -0.3% and still below its monthly level.

Resource equities are being liquidated faster than the metals themselves — copper +0.4% and gold -0.9%, yet COPX -6.3%, FCX -7.0%, GDX -6.0%, GDXJ -6.0%, NEM -6.0%, EZA -5.5%. That is de-grossing, not a commodity call.
Asia semis keep breaking: TAIEX -4.4% today, -17.0% monthly at z=-3.11 (acc -1.76), EWT -11.4% on the week, SMH -16.2% monthly, NVDA -30.5% and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range.

Passive tightening continues: 10y at 5.10% (+12bp on the week), 30y 5.46%, real yield 2.89% at the 95th percentile while 10y breakevens sit at 2.19 (3rd percentile) — and 2s10s at 27bp is flattening with acceleration -1.02.

trades.name: Short the Brazil complex into the BRL spiral
trades.line: Short EWZ vs long USDBRL: real in free fall, z=4.78
trades.expr: Short EWZ outright (or Jan 28-strike puts); fund half the notional with a long 1-month USD/BRL NDF. Size for gap risk — this is an accelerating move, not a value trade.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the pressure valve for a world of 5.10% US 10s, 2.89% real yields and collapsing commodity export revenue. A 17.1% one-month currency move with acceleration z=3.64 is a funding event; local equity in dollars keeps compounding the FX loss. Nothing in the data says it has stopped.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +2.1% today to 5.897 after a one-day pause, z=4.78; EWZ -3.1% to 30.07, -28.3% on the month (z=-3.62, acc -3.36), 0th percentile; Bovespa -19.4% monthly at z=-3.68. USDMXN +2.6% and EWW -4.2% say the stress is regional.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.55 or EWZ reclaiming 33 — that would mean local authorities or carry buyers have stabilised the move.
trades.target: EWZ toward 26 with USDBRL 6.40; roughly +15% on the combined book.

trades.name: Gasoline rebate over AI capex
trades.line: Long XRT vs short SMH: pump savings beat silicon
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral: long XRT, short SMH in equal notional. Roll monthly; add on any SMH bounce back toward its 200-day.
trades.thesis: A 20% one-month collapse in gasoline and a 29bp drop in mortgage rates is a direct, measurable transfer to the US household, and the retail tape is already printing it. Meanwhile the semiconductor complex is unwinding from a 54% one-year run with Taiwan leading it lower. The disinflation that hurts the capex trade is the same disinflation that pays the consumer.
trades.trigger: XRT +2.3% today with XRT/SPY at z=1.86, XLY +1.8%, TGT +4.0%, AMZN +3.8%; against SMH -16.2% on the month (SMH/SPY z=-2.01, 12.2% below its 200-day), TAIEX -4.4% today at z=-3.11 and NVDA at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY reclaiming its 200-day, or XRT losing 86 — that would say the consumer bid was just a short-cover.
trades.target: +12% on the pair as XRT/SPY extends toward its 52-week high and SMH retests 400.

trades.name: Oil equities still haven't finished catching down
trades.line: Short XOP: crude -17.7% m/m, E&Ps only -14%
trades.expr: Short XOP, or buy Feb 160/145 put spreads. Keep it small relative to the book — this is a short on a sector that is still above its 200-day.
trades.thesis: Crude is down 17.7% in a month and gasoline 20%, with WTI at a one-month z of -1.78 and DBC at -2.62. XLE is still 3.8% above its 200-day and XOP only 0.4% below. The equity hasn't marked to the strip; today was the first real session of catch-down and it came on a day when crude actually rose.
trades.trigger: XOP -3.4%, XOM -4.0%, CVX -4.0%, XLE -3.3% while WTI printed +0.6%; XOP one-month z=-1.72 with acceleration -1.31 and relative strength -9.7%; OIH -16.2% over three months.
trades.stop: WTI back above $90 (Brent $97) or XOP through 183 — a supply shock reverses the entire thesis.

trades.name: Own the belly — all the yield is real now
trades.line: Long IEF: 10y breakevens 3rd pctile, real yield 95th
trades.expr: Long IEF outright (or 10-year note futures). Fund partially by staying short high-beta equity rather than by shorting the long end — the 30y at 5.46% has its own supply problem.
trades.thesis: The 10-year real yield at 2.89% is in the 95th percentile and 27.9% above its 200-day, while 10-year breakevens at 2.19 sit in the 3rd percentile. That combination is passive tightening into a growth pulse of -10, and broad commodities at a one-month z of -2.62 say the inflation impulse the front end is pricing isn't coming. Bond vol is already cooperating.
trades.trigger: Yields fell across the curve today (2y -3bp, 5y -3bp, 10y -2bp, real -3bp) with MOVE -3.6% to 94.66 and -6.9% on the month; 2s10s at 27bp with acceleration -1.02; DBC -12.4% monthly; IEF +1.0% on the month off a 31st-percentile base.
trades.stop: 10-year above 5.25% or breakevens turning back up through 2.35 — that means a term-premium/supply problem, not a growth problem.
trades.target: 10-year back to 4.80%, roughly +4% total return on IEF.

trades.name: Buy the tail nobody owns
trades.line: Long SPLV vs short SPHB; SKEW z=-1.78 into 94th-pctile HY
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral long SPLV / short SPHB, overlaid with Jan SPX 5%/12% OTM put spreads — cheap skew means the wings fund themselves.
trades.thesis: Spot vol fell 8.6% today but nothing in the underlying stress resolved: HY OAS is still at the 94th percentile, BBB at a one-month z of 1.11, and the periphery is dislocating. Meanwhile SKEW collapsed 11.8% on the month to a z of -1.78 with acceleration -1.92 — the market has stopped paying for crash protection into a widening spread cycle. That is the asymmetry.
trades.trigger: VIX -8.6% to 22.44 with VIX3M at 24.29; SKEW 142.84 at z=-1.78; SPHB/SPLV -13.5% on the month (z=-2.13) and still rolling over; MTUM -11.8% monthly at z=-2.18; UNH -10.2% in a single session shows gap risk is already live.
trades.stop: SPHB/SPLV reclaiming 1.78 or VIX sustained below 17 with HY OAS back inside 3.20.
trades.target: +9% on the cash pair; the option overlay is the convexity, not the carry.

trades.name: Leadership has emigrated to India
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWT: +8.6% vs -17.3% on the month
trades.expr: Equal-notional long INDA / short EWT. Scale in on any Taiwan bounce; India is the cheap-oil, strong-currency, domestic-demand side of the same trade.
trades.thesis: Cheap crude and a firming rupee are a pure terms-of-trade windfall for India at exactly the moment Taiwan carries the entire AI de-rating. Both legs are trending hard in the right direction with acceleration confirming, and the pair is a cleaner expression of the global rotation than long EM outright, where Latin America is on fire.
trades.trigger: Sensex +1.2% today and +12.4% on the month at z=2.95 with acceleration 2.27, INDA relative strength +14.0%/+9.1% turning up, USDINR -1.8% at z=-1.86; against TAIEX -4.4% today, -17.0% monthly at z=-3.11, EWT -11.4% on the week and relative strength -13.2%.
trades.stop: -6% on the pair, or EWT reclaiming its 200-day with SMH/SPY turning up — the AI trade bottoming ends the short side.
trades.target: +12% as India's monthly relative strength extends and Taiwan retests the September lows.

trades.name: Short the crypto leverage, not the coin
trades.line: Short MSTR vs long IBIT: premium bleed, -33.6% monthly
trades.expr: Short MSTR against a long IBIT leg of equal notional. This isolates the equity premium and the balance-sheet leverage from the bitcoin price itself.
trades.thesis: Bitcoin bounced today and the levered proxies still fell. That is the classic sequence: when the coin stops falling and the equity keeps falling, the premium is being marked down and the financing channel is closing. Crypto remains the purest read on marginal leverage in the system, and it is still deteriorating faster than the underlying.
trades.trigger: BTC +1.4%, ETH +1.9%, SOL +2.0% today, yet MSTR -6.4% and COIN -3.9%; MSTR -33.6% on the month versus IBIT -23.6%, MSTR at the 6th percentile, COIN at the 0th.
trades.stop: BTC back above 75,000 with MSTR outperforming IBIT by 10% — a genuine risk-appetite turn reopens the issuance window.
trades.target: +15% on the pair as the equity premium compresses further.
